What did you think of 12 angry men?

Fonda sticks out, at first, as an irritating, sore thumb. The heavy mid-Atlantic drawl not helping in any way. Time passes, and the jurors' conclave start feeling the heat. We are drawn in, more and more as they start fumbling and breaking up, as the camera passes from one juror to the next. The kid's fate, hangs by a fine thread (literally, and figuratively). Suddenly, you no longer are in the room, you start feeling the oppressive heat, the tension, the conflicts, and want to get this over and done with.

Hell of a movie.

This is one of the greatest films ever made.

In my opinion its a great example of cinematography and mise-en-scène. Cinematography is not just Lawrence of Arabia (even though it is a great example). The perma-ban on death seems to me, will be the main reason this game will die quickly.

I love the idea (especially the aspect of spectating being part of the experience) but I think when it comes to the never being allowed to play the game again after death, players will quickly get bored.

I think a much better solution is to have a "pay to play" kinda system where you can spectate and build your character (like the dev said) but if you want to play, you have to pay a fee (maybe like $2) and you get entered into the player pool. When a player dies someone from the player pool is selected to play, when you die you are kicked out of the player pool and have to pay again to re-enter it (maybe also have it so that they have to wait 24 hrs before re-entering).

That way people can spectate and participate in the game, if they feel like playing they can pay and maybe have their turn, and after they die, they have the option of going again if they enjoyed their last play.

TL:DR Instead of a perma-ban on death, rather have a paid player pool (for people who want a turn to play the game) and on death have the person kicked out of the player pool with an option to re-enter.
